chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The ablution before the meal: the owner of the house begins, so that one person is not embarrassed. So when they finish from the meal, he begins with the one on his right, whether he be a freeman or a slave.

He said, 'And in another Hadith: First the lord of the house washes his hand, then he begins with the one on his right. And when the meal is raised, he begins with the one on the left of the owner of the house, and the last one to wash his hand will be the owner of the house, because he is more deserving of patience with the stains.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْبَيْتِ: The owner of the house / host

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for the host regarding ablution and hand washing before and after a meal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the etiquette of handwashing before and after meals, emphasizing the host's role in facilitating comfort for guests. The host washes first to avoid embarrassing guests and last to endure the mess (*ghamar*), reflecting a practical application of humility and service. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on social grace and the spiritual dimension of daily acts like eating.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ajlan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The ablution before the meal, the owner of the house begins, perhaps someone is embarrassed. So when (everyone) is free from the meal, he begins with the one on his right of the owner of the house, be he a freeman or a slave’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And in another Hadeeth: ‘First the lord of the house would wash his hands, then he would begin with the upon his right. And when the meal is raised, he would begin with the one upon his left of the owner of the house, and it would happen that the last one to wash his hands would be the owner of the house, because he was the first with the patience upon the stains’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ‘ Ajlan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The host must begin wudu so that no one feels shy. After eating food the person on the right of the host begins it, regardless of being a free or a slave . 5
He (the narrator) has said that in another Hadith it says, ‘The first before food and the last after food to wash should be the owner of the house, because he can remain patient with food stains. 5 ”
